standard_prerequisites: Rational equivalence by locally finite sums of divisors of rational functions on integral closed subspaces of one dimension higher, and the definition of the cap operation with a first Chern class
The compatibility of the cap operation with proper pushforward, which allows a computation on a coproduct to descend
The commutativity of the caps with two invertible sheaves on an integral space, and the additivity of the cap operation in the invertible sheaf
core_obligations: Unwind rational equivalence: the cycle is the sum of pushforwards of principal divisors from a locally finite family of integral closed subspaces one dimension higher

Recognise the coproduct of those subspaces as a proper cover of the space, write the cycle as the pushforward of the sum of the principal divisors on the coproduct, and use the compatibility of the cap operation with proper pushforward to reduce to the coproduct
Reduce further to an integral space carrying the divisor of a single rational function

Regard that rational function as a meromorphic section of the structure sheaf, take the divisor of a meromorphic section of the given invertible sheaf, and use the commutativity of the two caps on an integral space to identify the cap of the given sheaf with the cap of the structure sheaf
Conclude that the result vanishes, because the first Chern class of the structure sheaf is trivial and the cap operation is additive in the sheaf
proof_roadmap: Reduce a rationally trivial cycle to the coproduct of the subspaces occurring in its rational equivalence
Reduce to an integral space and a single rational function
Swap the given invertible sheaf for the structure sheaf through commutativity of caps and finish by additivity
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is that the operation of capping with a first Chern class is well defined on rational equivalence classes at source lines 3326-3335, label lemma-factors, whose proof occupies source lines 3337-3370. The proof is a reduction in two steps: a rationally trivial cycle is written as the pushforward of a sum of principal divisors from the coproduct of the subspaces occurring in the rational equivalence, and the compatibility of the cap operation with proper pushforward descends the claim to that coproduct, after which only an integral space carrying the divisor of one rational function remains. The final step is an identification rather than a computation: the rational function is viewed as a meromorphic section of the structure sheaf and the commutativity of caps on an integral space replaces the given invertible sheaf by the structure sheaf, whose first Chern class is trivial, the last step using additivity in the sheaf. The counted statement records neither the coproduct reduction nor the identification.
